documents.title: 323 Instructional and Assignment Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: Board-approved policy (effective June 2025) that gives each faculty member discretion to set GAI standards for their course sections. Where an instructor is silent, GAI may not be used for graded work. It also bars outsourcing assignment work to GAI, protects confidential data, allows faculty and staff use within limits, and routes misuse to the misconduct policy.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no uniform rule but says "individual faculty members have the discretion to set standards and procedures for the use of GAI tools", and students "may use GAI tools when permitted by faculty-specified standards". It has a fallback ban, but the main decision is delegated, so delegates.

documents.title: 312 Academic Misconduct
documents.summary: University procedure for handling faculty allegations of student academic misconduct. Its only AI content is one definitional line that counts unauthorized use of AI software as plagiarism, which Policy 323 relies on for enforcement.
documents.stance_why: The only AI statement says plagiarism "includes the unauthorized use of paraphrasing tools or text spinners and artificial intelligence software", so AI is barred unless authorized, which is restrict for the work the policy governs.

units.why: The definition says plagiarism "also includes the unauthorized use of paraphrasing tools or text spinners and artificial intelligence software", so unauthorized AI use is classified as misconduct (P36). The word "unauthorized" makes AI use restricted to what is authorized.
units.anchor: unauthorized use of paraphrasing tools or “text spinners” and artificial intelligence software

units.policy: Plagiarism includes the unauthorized use of paraphrasing tools or text spinners and artificial intelligence software
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on type P36 and unit_stance restrict; modality differed (A informs, B must-not). The sentence defines what plagiarism includes and gives no order to students, so informs.
units.fit_note: Also covers paraphrasing tools and text spinners.

documents.resolution_why: Coder A: delegates (not an AI policy, sets no AI stance of its own); coder B: restrict. The one AI sentence classes 'unauthorized use of ... artificial intelligence software' as plagiarism, so AI is barred unless authorized, which for the work this procedure governs is restrict.
